stages.title: Language sounds and pronunciation
stages.hook: Greek words carry a little mark above one vowel. What do you think it tells you?
explain: In Modern Greek every word with two or more syllables has an accent mark ´ above its stressed vowel. It shows which syllable is said louder: μαμά (mamá), νερό (neró), γάλα (gála). If you put the stress on the wrong syllable, people may find the word hard to understand.
Greek spelling often has several ways to write the same sound. The letters η, ι, υ and the pairs ει and οι all sound like "ee". The pair αι sounds like "e". So ναι (yes) is said "ne", not "nai".
stages.mnemonic: The little accent is a pointer: say this syllable loudest.

gq.q: What does the accent mark in νερό show?
o: That the word is a question
gq.why: In Modern Greek the accent marks the stressed syllable.

gq.q: How is the Greek letter χ in όχι pronounced?
gq.why: Greek χ is a breathy sound from the back of the mouth.

panel.q: Why is ναι (yes) said "ne"?
o: The letters are said in reverse
panel.why: In Modern Greek the combination αι is pronounced like e in "bed".

panel.q: Why do η, ι, υ, ει and οι all sound "ee"?
o: They are all the same letter
Sounds merged over centuries while spelling kept the old forms
Spelling was invented recently by chance
panel.why: Historical sound changes produced several spellings for one sound.

panel.q: Since 1982 Greek uses one accent mark instead of several. What is this system called?
panel.why: Monotonic Greek keeps the acute accent for stress. Older polytonic Greek had several marks.

teach.model: Every Greek word of two or more syllables has an accent mark on the stressed vowel. Several letters and pairs, such as η, ι, υ, ει and οι, sound like "ee". Learn the stress with the word.

points.ask: Do different letters sound the same?
Can you give a word example?

trip.prompt: Find the table of vowels and look at how many spellings give the sound "ee".

stages.title: Alphabet, script or basic characters
stages.hook: The word "alphabet" itself comes from the first two Greek letters. Can you guess which ones?
explain: The Greek alphabet has 24 letters. "Alphabet" comes from alpha (α) and beta (called vita today, β). Many letters look like English ones, but some are false friends: β is v, ρ is r, and ν is n.
Some letters are new sounds: δ is a soft "th" as in "this", θ is a hard "th" as in "think", γ is a soft rough "gh" and λ is l. The letter σ is written ς at the end of a word.
stages.mnemonic: Alpha and vita start the alphabet. Remember that β says v!

gq.q: How many letters does the Greek alphabet have?
What sound does β stand for in Modern Greek?
gq.why: The letter vita β is pronounced v today. The sound b is written μπ.

panel.q: Why do mathematicians and scientists use letters like π, α and Δ?
o: Greek letters are the only ones that computers can read
They are shorter than Latin letters
The Greek alphabet gives extra symbols and has a long tradition in science
English has no letters for them
panel.why: Greek letters are a ready set of symbols used in mathematics and science since ancient times.

panel.q: Why does σ change to ς at the end of a word?
o: It is a different letter with a different sound
It is a position-based form of the same letter
panel.why: Sigma has two written forms for one sound.

panel.q: Why does English use the word "alphabet"?
o: It was borrowed from Greek α and β via Latin
It was invented in the 20th century
It names the first two Latin letters only
panel.why: Greek α and β were used to name the whole set of letters.

teach.model: Greek has 24 letters. It gave us the word alphabet from alpha and beta. Some letters are false friends: β is v and ρ is r. Sigma has a final form ς.

points.ask: Where does the word alphabet come from?

trip.prompt: Find the table of letters and say each letter name aloud once.

stages.title: Greetings and introductions
stages.hook: Greeks say Γεια σου to a friend. Which small word do you change for a teacher?
explain: Γεια σου (ya su) means "hello" or "goodbye" to a friend. For one person you do not know, or several people, say Γεια σας (ya sas). Use Καλημέρα in the morning, Καλησπέρα in the evening and Καληνύχτα at night.
To say your name, use Με λένε, which means "they call me". To ask a friend, say Πώς σε λένε; The Greek question mark looks like an English semicolon (;).
stages.mnemonic: Σου is for you, σας is for respect.

gq.q: You meet your new teacher. Which greeting is better?
gq.why: Σας is the polite form for people you do not know well.

gq.q: What does the Greek question mark look like?
gq.why: Greek uses ; to end a question.

panel.q: The word γεια comes from an old word for "health". What does this suggest?
o: It is a loan from English
It is a verb for walking
The greeting once meant wishing someone good health
panel.why: Γεια σου literally wishes health to you.

panel.q: Καλημέρα is made of καλή and ημέρα. What does that show?
o: Greek greetings often wish a "good day", built from two words
panel.why: Καλή means good and ημέρα means day.

panel.q: It is 9 pm. Which greeting fits when you arrive at a friend's house?
panel.why: Καλησπέρα is used from the afternoon to the evening.

teach.model: Say Γεια σου to a friend and Γεια σας to someone you respect. Use Καλημέρα in the morning and Καλησπέρα in the evening. Say Με λένε and your name.

points.ask: How do I give my name?
When do I use the polite form?

trip.prompt: Find examples of everyday greetings and note one you could use today.

stages.title: Numbers and counting
stages.hook: Many English words like "triangle" and "octopus" hide Greek numbers. Can you spot them?
explain: Count in Greek: ένα, δύο, τρία, τέσσερα, πέντε, έξι, επτά, οκτώ. Then come εννιά (9) and δέκα (10).
Ένα, τρία and τέσσερα have different forms for masculine, feminine and neuter. One is ένας, μία and ένα. Three is τρεις with masculine and feminine, but τρία with neuter. Δύο does not change.
stages.mnemonic: Tri-angle has tria, octo-pus has okto: the numbers are inside English words.

gq.q: How do you say "three cats" (γάτες is feminine)?
gq.why: Three takes τρεις with masculine and feminine nouns.

gq.q: Which form means "one" with a feminine noun?
gq.why: One is ένας, μία, ένα for masculine, feminine and neuter.

panel.q: Why does Greek have different forms for "one", "three" and "four" but not for "two"?
o: Some numbers decline for gender and others are fixed by history of the language
Greek counts only up to two
panel.why: The forms of numbers differ: δύο is invariable.

panel.q: English "octopus" means "eight feet". Which Greek number is inside?
panel.why: Octo comes from Greek οκτώ.

panel.q: In "Είμαι οκτώ χρονών", what does χρονών mean?
panel.why: Χρονών is the genitive plural of χρόνος, used to give age.

teach.model: The numbers are ένα, δύο, τρία, τέσσερα, πέντε, έξι, επτά, οκτώ. One, three and four change by gender: ένας, μία, ένα; τρεις, τρία. Δύο stays the same.

trip.prompt: Find English words that come from Greek numbers and list two.

stages.title: Colours and shapes
stages.hook: The sea in Greece looks blue. Which of two Greek words for blue would you use?
explain: Colour words are adjectives that match the noun: κόκκινος (masculine), κόκκινη (feminine) and κόκκινο (neuter). The dictionary list is often given in the neuter: κόκκινο, κίτρινο, πράσινο, άσπρο, μαύρο.
Greek has two blues: μπλε is dark blue and does not change, and γαλάζιο is light blue like the sky. The sound b is written μπ. Shapes: κύκλος (circle), τετράγωνο (square).
stages.mnemonic: Red apple, red ball, red sun: κόκκινο, κόκκινη, κόκκινος. The ending follows the noun.

gq.q: Which is correct for "the red ball" (η μπάλα is feminine)?
gq.why: The adjective takes the feminine form κόκκινη.
Γαλάζιο is light blue; μπλε is dark blue.

panel.q: Why is the word μπλε written with μπ?
o: Greek writes the sound b with the pair μπ
panel.why: The letter β says v, so b is written μπ in borrowed words and some Greek words.

panel.q: Why do κόκκινος, κόκκινη and κόκκινο differ?
o: The adjective matches the gender of its noun
panel.why: Greek adjectives agree in gender, number and case.

panel.q: Why does μπλε not change before different nouns?
o: It is a borrowed word that is invariable
panel.why: Some loan words, like μπλε, have one fixed form.

teach.model: Greek colours are adjectives that match the noun: κόκκινος, κόκκινη, κόκκινο. The blue words are μπλε for dark blue and γαλάζιο for light blue.

trip.prompt: Compare how languages divide blue and find the Greek example.

stages.title: Family and people
stages.hook: In Greece many people celebrate a "name day". Do you know what it is?
explain: Family words are: μαμά, μπαμπάς, αδελφός (brother), αδελφή (sister), γιαγιά, παππούς, οικογένεια and φίλος (friend). Every noun has a gender and an article: ο for masculine, η for feminine and το for neuter.
To say "my", put μου after the noun: η γιαγιά μου. Many Greeks celebrate a name day (γιορτή), the feast day of the saint they are named after.
stages.mnemonic: Μου follows the noun: μαμά μου, "my mum".

gq.why: Γιαγιά is feminine, so it takes η.

o: A day for naming a baby
A day when you change your name
A celebration on the feast day of the saint you are named after
gq.why: Name days are widely celebrated in Greece, sometimes more than birthdays.

panel.q: Why is it η γιαγιά μου and not μου η γιαγιά?
o: In Greek the short possessive comes after the noun
panel.why: The weak possessive μου follows the noun phrase.

panel.q: Why does Greek use an article with names of family members, as in η μαμά?
o: It shows the speaker is a child
Greek uses the definite article more often than English
panel.why: The definite article often appears where English leaves it out.

panel.q: Why do we say Έχω έναν αδελφό with έναν and not ένας?
o: The object takes the accusative case
panel.why: Ένας becomes έναν in the accusative masculine.

teach.model: Use μαμά, μπαμπάς, αδελφός, αδελφή, γιαγιά and παππούς. Nouns have ο, η or το. Say μου after the noun for "my": η γιαγιά μου.

points.ask: What are ο, η and το?

trip.prompt: Find out how name days are celebrated in Greece.

stages.title: Common objects
stages.hook: In Greek you often say "the" before things. How do you say "the door"?
explain: Greek nouns have three genders: masculine with ο, feminine with η and neuter with το. Examples: η πόρτα (the door), η καρέκλα (the chair), το τραπέζι (the table), το βιβλίο (the book).
The verb "to be" is είναι for he, she, it and they: Αυτό είναι το βιβλίο means "This is the book". To say "on the table" use στο τραπέζι, where σε (in, on, at) joins with το to make στο.
stages.mnemonic: Σε plus το becomes στο, as two friends hugging into one.
sentences: The book is on the table.

gq.why: Τραπέζι is neuter, like most nouns ending in -ι.
Πόρτα is feminine, so it takes η.

panel.q: Why do we say στο τραπέζι, not σε το τραπέζι?
o: σε and το merge into στο
panel.why: The preposition σε blends with the article.

panel.q: Why does the accent move in τηλέφωνό μου?
o: A word with the stress on the third-last syllable gets an extra accent when μου follows
panel.why: Stress rules require an extra accent on the noun before a weak pronoun.

panel.q: Why can a Greek learner not guess gender only by meaning?
o: Gender is grammatical and not always tied to meaning
panel.why: Learn each noun with its article, such as το παράθυρο.

teach.model: Greek nouns have ο, η or το for masculine, feminine and neuter. Learn the article with the noun: η πόρτα, το βιβλίο. Σε plus το becomes στο.

points.ask: What are the little words in front?
How do I say "on the table"?

trip.prompt: Find the three genders in Greek and a noun for each.

stages.title: Everyday actions
stages.hook: The Greek verb "I read" is just one word. Where did "I" go?
explain: Greek verbs change their ending for each person. For διαβάζω (I read): διαβάζω, διαβάζεις, διαβάζει, διαβάζουμε, διαβάζετε, διαβάζουν. The ending shows the person, so Greeks usually leave out the pronoun.
Other verbs: γράφω (I write), παίζω (I play), κοιμάμαι (I sleep), πίνω (I drink), τρώω (I eat), ακούω (I listen), μιλάω (I speak). In Greek dictionaries the verb is listed in the "I" form.
stages.mnemonic: Ending -ω is "I", -εις is "you", -ει is "he or she".
sentences: The children play in the yard.

gq.q: Which form means "he or she reads"?
gq.why: The third person singular ends in -ει.

gq.q: What does Πίνω νερό mean without a pronoun?
gq.why: The ending -ω shows the first person singular.

panel.q: Why can Greek drop the pronoun εγώ?
o: The verb ending already shows the person
panel.why: Endings like -ω identify the subject.

panel.q: Why do dictionaries list Greek verbs as "I" forms?
o: Greek verbs have one form only
panel.why: The ancient infinitive disappeared; the first person singular is the citation form.

panel.q: Why is the verb in Τα παιδιά παίζουν plural?
o: It agrees with the plural subject
Plural verbs are always used for children
panel.why: Subject and verb agree in number.

teach.model: Greek verbs end differently for each person: διαβάζω, διαβάζεις, διαβάζει. The ending shows who does it, so the pronoun is often dropped. Dictionaries list the "I" form.

points.ask: Do I need to say εγώ?

trip.prompt: Find the present tense endings and compare two persons.

stages.title: Simple listening and speaking
stages.hook: What can you say in Greek when you hear fast speech and need help?
explain: To check understanding, say Δεν καταλαβαίνω (I do not understand) or Καταλαβαίνω (I understand). Ask Πιο αργά, παρακαλώ (slower, please) or Ξανά, παρακαλώ (again, please).
Τι κάνεις; means "How are you?" and a common answer is Είμαι καλά, ευχαριστώ. Yes/no questions have the same words as statements: the voice goes up. Writing uses ; for a question mark.
stages.mnemonic: Slow, again, thank you: three little phrases keep a chat going.

gq.why: Τι κάνεις; asks how you are.

gq.q: How do you ask someone to repeat?

panel.q: Why does Greek use ; as a question mark?
o: It is the Greek convention for the question mark
panel.why: Greek writing uses ; for questions.

panel.q: How can a yes/no question be made from a statement?
panel.why: Intonation marks the question.

panel.q: A stranger asks something and you do not follow. Which is polite?
panel.why: Συγγνώμη and παρακαλώ keep it polite.

teach.model: Say Δεν καταλαβαίνω if you do not understand, and ask Πιο αργά, παρακαλώ or Ξανά, παρακαλώ. Answer Τι κάνεις; with Είμαι καλά, ευχαριστώ.

points.ask: How do I say I do not understand?
How do I ask for slower speech?
How do I ask how someone is?

trip.prompt: Find a short sound sample or phrase list and repeat two phrases aloud.
